subject.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs

question: Should ClawHub resolution, bundled manifest ID/path/package mappings, and official catalog ID/package mappings bypass arbitrary-source acknowledgement, while every other direct first install requires confirmation or `--acknowledge-non-clawhub-install`?
rationale: The patch and proof establish consistent enforcement, but repository automation cannot decide which executable-code authorities OpenClaw should designate as trusted or whether breaking existing noninteractive arbitrary-source installs is acceptable.

options.title: Approve the proposed trust matrix
options.body: Accept the current trusted-source exemptions and require the new flag for arbitrary noninteractive first installs.

options.title: Narrow the trusted exemptions
options.body: Require explicit acknowledgement for one or more ClawHub, bundled, or official-catalog source forms currently exempted.

options.title: Preserve compatibility by default
options.body: Keep existing noninteractive behavior and expose strict arbitrary-source acknowledgement as an opt-in policy instead.

recommendation.title: Approve the proposed trust matrix
recommendation.body: Accept the current trusted-source exemptions and require the new flag for arbitrary noninteractive first installs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR, carried the complete implementation, and have prior merged history in the same ClawHub install-trust paths; adjacent history owners should be consulted for final approval.
